# Native OpenSim Source-Body Inertia Admission

Issue #12191 adds a read-only gate between an OpenSim source model and a
physical forward-dynamics claim. It uses the coordinate-invariant principal
moment validator from #12183, then binds every declared `Body` mass, mass
center, and six inertia entries to a fresh native OpenSim readback. The gate
does not alter source XML, project tensors, scale anatomy, or optimize a model.

## Source, Frame, and Native Readback

The admitted source is one hash-bound `.osim` file with an explicit `BodySet`
inventory. Each body supplies mass in kg, center of mass in its body frame in
m, and the symmetric inertia about that center in kg m². For source entries
`(Ixx,Iyy,Izz,Ixy,Ixz,Iyz)`, the audited tensor is

$$I=\begin{bmatrix}
I_{xx}&I_{xy}&I_{xz}\\ I_{xy}&I_{yy}&I_{yz}\\ I_{xz}&I_{yz}&I_{zz}
\end{bmatrix}. $$

The parser rejects missing, duplicate, nonfinite or malformed body properties.
Source and freshly initialized native body names must agree exactly; every
mass, center and inertia component must read back exactly. A source-byte
change during admission also rejects. The receipt binds the source, adapter
and three installed OpenSim native binary digests. This is a body-property
gate; external model assets and complete numerical restart require their
separate source-closure and replay policies.

Positive-mass bodies must pass the shared finite, symmetric,
strictly-positive-principal-moment and triangle checks. The helper's existing
absolute $10^{-9}$ kg m² numerical floor is a declared limitation, not a
material uncertainty interval. An exact zero-mass, zero-inertia body may be
admitted as a native internal/welded routing carrier; zero mass with nonzero
inertia rejects. Native OpenSim itself rejects an external free/moving
massless body. No epsilon mass or inertia is introduced.

## Exact 557-Muscle Diagnostic Result

The derived BUET–Hamner XML SHA-256
`453e09c4e42dcc3f4b74a3b2efeff063e96c3820b3eee1efe95eef249579010d`
has 40 source/native bodies. Nine exact massless routing carriers pass the
separate zero policy. Four positive-mass bodies—bilateral clavicles and
scapulae—fail the necessary principal-moment condition; the other 27 bodies
pass this numeric gate. The four failures are inherited from the retained
author-published upper/trunk donor, and native OpenSim 4.6 reads their source
tensors exactly. The complete source and runtime identities, tests and failure
names are in the public receipt and retained read-only provenance review.

This blocks **physical admission** of that 557-muscle parameterization. Its
0.2 ms saved-excitation replay remains a labeled diagnostic, and the failed
1 ms chart run remains retained. A passing body gate on another source would
still leave anatomy, passive-force physiology, assistance, native contact and
grip, full-horizon replay, capture registration and all 17 variants across six
ecosystems open. Neither a positive full-system mass matrix nor Moco
initialization overrides an invalid individual source body. Publication is
blocked until the governed calculation and scientific approvals are complete.
